prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The sequence shows an indoor clothing area with racks and hanging garments extending across the middle and right; several people occupy different depths, from a small figure roughly 4–6 m away at far left to prominent figures about 0.7–2 m ahead in later frames. From left to right in time, the wearer appears to move or turn rightward and closer to the central person and garments: a person shifts from roughly 2–3 m away near center-left to about 1–1.5 m ahead, while a pale garment enters the foreground within about 0.3–0.7 m and occludes much of that person. In the last frame, a person at center-right is about 1–1.5 m away, with a garment and rack within arm’s reach of that person and approximately 0.5–1 m from the wearer; another person is only partly visible at the far right edge. Brightness separates near garments and bodies from darker walls, windows, and recesses more clearly than RGB alone, but some people and clothing have similar depth values, boundaries bleed together, and exact metric distances cannot be recovered reliably from this monocular map.
descriptions.segmentation: The maps isolate multiple people against the clothing-store interior: a distant person at far left, another around center-left, a larger nearby person near center, and one or more people to the right, with two suitcase-labelled regions at the extreme right that appear spatially associated with foreground racks or garments. Across the five frames, the dominant person mask grows and shifts from center-left toward center/right, indicating decreasing camera distance from roughly 2–3 m to about 1 m, while a large foreground garment occludes the person in frame 4 and much of the lower scene in frame 5. The masks make overlapping silhouettes and partial edge visibility clearer than RGB—for example, the frame-4 person remains visible only as a narrow region beside or behind the foreground garment, and the final rightmost person is clipped by the image boundary. The map is unreliable for object identity and extent: most racks and garments are unlabelled, the suitcase labels likely cover ambiguous clothing/rack regions, some people merge with nearby items, and the masks provide no direct metric depth or dependable facing direction.
descriptions.pose: The skeletons locate articulated people even when texture and clothing obscure limbs: an upright distant person appears at far left, a compact or partially occluded person appears around center-left, a tall nearby body occupies the center, and later poses lie around center-right and the lower-right foreground. Over time the central body grows from roughly 1–2 m away to near foreground scale, while later skeletons shift right and become more horizontal or fragmented as people are occluded by garments, racks, or the frame boundary; the final lower-right limbs are roughly 0.5–1.5 m from the wearer and may be within the wearer’s arm’s reach at the nearest points. Joint geometry suggests some torsos are side-on or turned relative to the wearer, but missing facial landmarks and distorted limbs make it unsafe to determine consistently whether anyone is looking toward the camera; the RGB more clearly shows that the prominent orange-shirted person is generally side-facing before appearing more front-facing in the final frame. The pose map reveals approximate limb placement and reach that are hard to separate in RGB, but several skeletons are incomplete, displaced, or implausibly connected, hands are scarcely detected, and it cannot establish exact distances, object positions, or whether apparent overlaps are true contact.
